# Doublecheck benchmark

**Everything below is synthetic.** The scenarios are generated by `server/sim.ts` and `server/bench.ts` with fixed seeds, so the numbers are exactly repeatable (`npm run benchmark`). They describe how the rules behave on these generated scenario sets. They are not measurements of real homes, real sensors or real appliances, and they should not be read as real-world accuracy.

## 1. Contradiction (valve reports closed; flow meter says otherwise)

5000 scenarios per configuration (500 per class, 10 classes). "Broken" means water is really still flowing in the scenario.

| Class | World | Verdict with 1 flow meter (Worked / Problem / Not verified) | with 2 independent sensors |
|---|---|---|---|
| closed_clean | fine | 500 / 0 / 0 | 500 / 0 / 0 |
| closed_noisy | fine (readings near the limit) | 397 / 9 / 94 | 275 / 1 / 224 |
| stuck_open | broken | 0 / 500 / 0 | 0 / 500 / 0 |
| partial_leak | broken (small leak) | 0 / 500 / 0 | 0 / 498 / 2 |
| dead_sensor | either; sensor silent | 0 / 0 / 500 | 0 / 0 / 500 |
| one_reading | either; one reading | 0 / 0 / 500 | 0 / 0 / 500 |
| late_only | either; only pre-settling readings | 0 / 0 / 500 | 0 / 0 / 500 |
| stale_open | broken; last reading 6 h old | 0 / 500 / 0 | 0 / 500 / 0 |
| stuck_zero_sensor | broken; one sensor stuck at 0 | 500 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 500 |
| sensors_disagree | either; sensors disagree | 0 / 500 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 500 |

| Rate | 1 sensor | 2 sensors |
|---|---|---|
| False reassurance, main set (broken, called Worked) | 0.0% | 0.0% |
| False reassurance, including a sensor stuck at zero | **15.5%** | 0.0% |
| False alarm (fine, called Problem found) | 0.51% | 0.05% |
| Detection of broken (called Problem found) | 73.3% | 60.0% |
| Not verified when broken (abstained) | 26.7% | 40.0% |

**Set definition.** The "main set" is every class except `stuck_zero_sensor`. Over that set, zero broken scenarios were called Worked. The `stuck_zero_sensor` class is shown separately because **one sensor stuck at zero looks exactly like a closed valve; a single flow meter cannot catch it.** With two independent sensors the disagreement is caught and the answer becomes Not verified. A zero rate here is a statement about this set, not a guarantee.

## 2. Gradual change (heating-draw time drifting over weeks)

60 simulated appliances per class, monitored every 3 days over 180–300 days of history. The model has a standing-loss term that varies per appliance (0–4 min), multiplicative noise (4–12%) and one or two cycles a day.

| Class | Truth | Alerted at least once | Final: Worked / Problem / Not verified |
|---|---|---|---|
| stable | no change | 0/60 | 60 / 0 / 0 |
| strong_seasonal | no change; inlet swings 20±(8–10) °C | 0/60 | 60 / 0 / 0 |
| setpoint_change | no change; target 50→60 °C | 0/60 | 60 / 0 / 0 |
| gradual_decline | heating time rises to 1.8–3.2× | 60/60 | 0 / 60 / 0 |
| step_change | jump to 1.7–2.3× | 60/60 | 0 / 60 / 0 |
| sparse_decline | declining, 75% of cycles missing | 28/60 | 0 / 28 / 32 |
| missing_temps_decline | declining, 65% of start temperatures missing | 0/60 | 0 / 0 / 60 |
| short_history | no change; 25 days of history | 0/60 | 0 / 0 / 60 |

- Detection (gradual + step classes): **100.0%**.
- False alarms on no-change classes: **0.0%** of appliances, 0.0% of checks.
- Median true degradation when the first alert fired: **1.46×** normal heating time.
- Median lead time (gradual class): **34 days** between the first alert and heating time reaching 2× normal (48 appliances).
- Declining appliances left as Worked (false reassurance): **0.0%**. Where there was too little data (sparse, missing temperatures) the answer was Not verified.
- Compaction agreement (daily summaries + 30 days raw vs all raw): **100.0%** of final verdicts.

Known limits: heating time is assumed to scale with the temperature rise within a window of ±8 °C; usage, tank size and appliance settings other than target temperature are not modelled; a baseline taken after the appliance had already degraded would hide the change.

## 3. Execution anomaly (a run that finished, but oddly)

1800 simulated runs (300 per class); each run is compared with 25 earlier runs of the same mode.

| Class | Called Problem | Called Worked | Not verified |
|---|---|---|---|
| normal | 0 | 300 | 0 |
| mild_variation | 0 | 300 | 0 |
| many_pauses | 300 | 0 | 0 |
| long_run | 300 | 0 | 0 |
| pauses_and_long | 300 | 0 | 0 |
| new_device | 0 | 0 | 300 |

- Detection of anomalous runs: **100.0%**; false alarm on normal and mildly varying runs: **0.0%**; anomalous runs called Worked: **0.0%**; new device (fewer than 6 earlier runs) → Not verified: **100%**.

## What this does not show

- Nothing here was run against a real home, real sensors or Alexa+.
- The generators encode my assumptions about how faults look. Real devices will behave differently.
- Rates on a synthetic set can be tuned to look good; that is why the classes where the engine is blind or abstains are listed rather than dropped.
- **These sets are not held out.** Two rules were corrected after early runs of this same benchmark exposed misses (a pause threshold that was too generous for skewed counts, and a baseline that could be contaminated by early drift or a short history). The test suite re-runs the benchmark on other seeds (3, 4, 5 and 9) with the same assertions, but the generators are still mine.
